## Chosen hook

Spoken: "Nine months ago somebody took my blood, and then told me a word. Normal. I never got told what it meant."
On-screen text (frame 1, muted-legible): "I got a word. Not an answer."
Archetype: Experimenter, with device 1 (ordinary build, then rupture) as a pause rather than a cut.

**Reframed 2026-07-31.** The original framing for this episode was a man testing himself for the first time and not knowing what would come back. That is no longer true and was never quite true: Keith was tested by the NHS on 7 October and 18 November 2025 and has the results. Writing it as a first look would have put a false line in his mouth on camera. The honest and better version is that he already has numbers, was given a word instead of an explanation, and is now doing it again with the thing he built to answer that.

## Script (part one, the observational half)

**Emotion:** Recognition / relief.

**Scope.** This is the half filmable on the day. It carries no results and no figures, because the Andro Prime numbers do not exist yet. Part two is cut in when they land, and the two publish as one episode. The split was decided 2026-07-28 and is what makes this shootable before results.

**Addiction loop.** Stakes: Keith has been sat with numbers for nine months that nobody explained, and there is a kit on the table. Big question: why is he doing this again when he already has results. Head fake: the viewer assumes the point is getting tested; the point is that he was already tested and it did not answer anything, which is a different problem entirely and the one the company exists for. Rehook: "so this is not me finding out whether something is wrong. It is me finding out what it means."

**Structure:** A, Personal story.

```
[0-5s]   Nine months ago somebody took my blood. Then they told me a
         word. Normal.
         [Visual: the unopened kit on the kitchen table, morning light.
         His hand comes in and turns it over.]
         [Text: I got a word. Not an answer.]

[5-16s]  I never got told what it meant. I got a range, and a number
         somewhere inside it, and that was the end of the conversation.
         [Slower]
         I did not feel normal. I felt flat, and I had done for a
         while.

[16-28s] So I am doing it again. Not because I think something is
         wrong. Because nobody has ever sat down and explained the
         numbers I already had.
         [opens the kit, lays the lancet out]

[28-42s] This is the whole thing. A lancet, a tube, and about six drops.
         Morning, before I have eaten, because the number moves through
         the day and you want it caught at the same point each time.
         [does the finger-prick on camera, unhurried, no music sting]
         [Pause]

[42-52s] That is it. Goes in the post today.
         [Slower]
         I built this company because I got a word when I wanted an
         explanation. Now I have to sit and wait like everybody else.

[CTA]    Next one is the numbers, and I have not seen them either.
         What did yours actually say?
         [Text: Education, not medical advice]
```

*Four-check: interesting to Mark, because it names the exact thing that happened to him, being handed a word instead of an answer. Compressed, roughly 50 seconds. The hook stands alone muted. End emotion is recognition. Compliance, stated as what the copy does: it describes a collection procedure and a morning routine; it explains why timing matters using the same diurnal-variation reasoning the lab itself printed; it discloses the founder at the turn; it ends on a question. It carries no figures, makes no statement about what any result will show, and keeps the supplement range out of shot entirely.*
